title: Kisii Banana Stew
author: Mama Akinyi

heritage.origin: Kisii County (Gusiiland) — Nyanza region, Western Kenya
heritage.history: The Gusii people of Nyanza are one of Kenya's most agriculturally productive communities. The fertile highlands of Kisii County receive abundant rainfall and produce bananas in extraordinary quantities. Green cooking bananas (matoke) are a staple food — steamed, stewed, or cooked in a spiced tomato sauce.
heritage.modernEvolution: Banana stew remains a daily staple in Gusiiland and is gaining appreciation as interest in regional Kenyan foods grows.

desc: Kisii Banana Stew — green cooking bananas (matoke) simmered in a rich tomato, onion, and garlic sauce with mild spices. A hearty, naturally starchy, deeply satisfying stew from the banana farms of the Kisii highlands.
longDesc: The Kisii highlands are blanketed in banana farms. Green matoke cooked in a spiced tomato sauce become beautifully tender and absorb the surrounding flavours while contributing their natural starchiness.
ingredients: 6 large green cooking bananas (matoke) — peeled and halved
steps: Peel bananas (wear gloves). Halve or cut into chunks.
Submerge in salted water immediately after peeling.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden — 6 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, and paprika. Cook for 6—8 minutes until thick.
Drain bananas and add to the pot. Stir to coat.
Add water. Bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer for 25—30 minutes until bananas are completely tender.
chefTips: Wear gloves when peeling green bananas — the latex sap stains permanently.
Keep peeled bananas in salted water — they brown rapidly.
Green matoke should be completely tender when done.
commonMistakes: Browning bananas — submerge immediately after peeling.
cookingScience: Green cooking bananas are high in resistant starch. During cooking, resistant starch partially converts to digestible starch and some dissolves into the sauce, naturally thickening it.
sustainabilityTips: Kisii County is one of Kenya's most productive agricultural areas.
healthBenefits: Rich in resistant starch — a prebiotic fibre.
Good source of potassium and vitamin B6.
culturalNote: Kisii banana stew is a daily expression of the Gusii community's deep relationship with their extraordinarily fertile land.
